items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the workers' compensation law, in relation to requiring the
workers' compensation board to appoint the uninsured employers' fund as the
insurance carrier in cases when the identity of the responsible insurance
carrier for the employer cannot be determined within ten days of the filing of
a claim and to proceed with hearings and provide notices necessary to process
such claim; and to make conforming technical changes
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6628

SPONSOR: SKOUFIS
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the workers' compensation law, in relation to requiring
the workers' compensation board to appoint the uninsured employers' fund
as the insurance carrier in cases when the identity of the responsible
insurance carrier for the employer cannot be determined within ten days
of the filing of a claim and to proceed with hearings and provide
notices necessary to process such claim; and to make conforming techni-
cal changes

 
PURPOSE:

To require the Workers' Compensation Board, if the Board is unable to
determine the identity of the responsible carrier within ten days of the
filing of a new claim, to appoint the Uninsured Employers' Fund

(UEF) as the temporary carrier until such time that the responsible
carrier for the employer is determined. Once the UEF is appointed as the
temporary carrier, the UEF shall immediately commence payments and
provide medical care in accordance with the Workers' Compensation Law.
Further, the Board shall immediately schedule a hearing with notice to
the employer by certified mail, return receipt requested, with a direc-
tion that the employer provide proof of having insurance in effect as of
the date of injury or date of disablement. The hearing would also deter-
mine the validity of the claim.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 20 of the Workers' Compensation Law is amended by adding a new
subdivision 1-a which provides that if the Workers' Compensation Board
is unable to determine the identity of the responsible insurance carrier
for the employer within ten days of the filing of a new claimant, the
Board, shall:

 
NEW SUBSECTION (a) appoint the Uninsured Employers' Fund as the insur-
ance carrier until such time as the identity of the responsible insur-
ance carrier for the employer is determined. Upon appointment, the Unin-
sured Employers' Fund shall immediately commence payments and provide
medical care in accordance with the Workers' Compensation Law; and

 
NEW SUBSECTION (b) schedule a hearing to determine the identity of the
responsible insurance carrier for the employer and to determine the
validity of such claim for compensation; and New Subsection (c) provide
notice of such claim and hearing to the employer by certified mail,
return receipt requested; with a direction that the employer provide
proof of having insurance in effect on the date of accident or date of
disablement.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Under the Workers' Compensation Law, when it is determined that an
employer did not have a valid Workers' Compensation insurance policy in
effect on the date of an accident or date of disablement, the Uninsured
Employers Fund (UEF) is named as the carrier. In that situation, the
employer is liable to reimburse the UEF for all costs incurred by the
UEF due to the claim. The determination of who should be the carrier
takes place after a number of hearings at which the employer can attend
and provide proof of insurance. Proof of payment of premium and proper
cancellation by the insurance company are the most litigated issues.
These hearings are held at least a month a part. There are usually 2 or
3 hearings to determine the proper carrier.

Unfortunately, the Workers' Compensation Board has not been scheduling
the first hearing to determine the proper carrier until a month to three
months after discovering that, according to the Board's records, there
is no carrier. It takes virtually no time to discover whether a carrier
is on record since the records are computerized.  There is no reason to
delay the hearings to determine the proper carrier.

During the time before a proper carrier is determined, the injured work-
er has a difficult time obtaining medical treatment since most doctors
do not want to treat someone who does not have a carrier with a carrier
case number. Also, the claimant will not receive any payments until the
proper carrier is determined.

This bill would correct this situation. If the Board is unable to deter-
mine the identity of the responsible carrier within ten days of the
filing of a new claimant, the Board shall appoint the UEF as the tempo-
rary carrier until such time that the responsible carrier for the
employer is determined. Once the UEF is appointed as the temporary
carrier, the UEF shall immediately commence payments and provide medical
care in accordance with the Workers' Compensation Law.

Further, the Board shall schedule a hearing with notice to the employer
by certified mail, return receipt requested with a direction that the
employer provide proof of having insurance in effect as of the date of
injury or date of disablement. The hearing would also determine the
validity of the claim.

In the event, that a carrier other than the UEF is determined to be the
responsible carrier, that carrier is responsible to reimburse the UEF
for expenses of medical treatment and lost time incurred while the UEF
was the temporary carrier.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019: A7404 - Referred to Labor

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately
